summary: German industrialist Alfred Hugenberg ran Krupp before the First World War, built a right-wing press empire that pushed endless war and the stab-in-the-back lie, led the nationalist DNVP and in 1933 helped make Hitler chancellor, briefly serving as his economics minister.

evidence.note: born June 1865 in Hanover, before German unification
co-founds the German General League in 1891, later renamed the Pan-German League
works for the Prussian Settlement Commission in Posen 1894-99, then runs settler co-ops there
hired by Gustav Krupp as board chairman in 1909; used as main_span start
Krupp arms-race sales tactics and the Kornwalzer bribery scandal implicating him
account of the Herero genocide in Namibia, massacres and poisoned wells, as his model for Africa
Pan-German propaganda rules out any peace that returns Belgium or French land
industry fund buys the August Scherl publishing house in 1916 under his control
buys up papers during hyperinflation and the largest cinema chain; top media magnate
becomes DNVP chairman in 1928 and pushes the party further right
deal: backs Hitler as chancellor in exchange for an economic superministry
forced out in June 1933; retires to his estate, arrested in 1949, dies March 1951

notes: Primary theme is a close call between propaganda-media (the press empire runs 1913-1933 across both parts) and nazism (the description pitches him as Hitler's enabler); nazism kept secondary. The host places the Hitler negotiations in late 1933, but the chancellorship deal was January 1933. Herero genocide is an illustrative segment of his colonial aims, so NA is not in the setting. Elon Musk comparisons are modern asides, not legacy.
